subject: Lifecore: hosting eligibility & audit evidence — post-call workplan
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@lifecore.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Lifecore: hosting eligibility & audit evidence — post-call workplan

Alex — thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on what will unblock Lifecore's hosting decision (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC).

Summary from call
- Primary constraint: PHI in production workflows; Lifecore must have a signed BAA and demonstrable controls for SOC 2 (security & availability).
- Preference: lean toward Dedicated if we can meet SLA/timestamping requirements; Private VPC considered for full network isolation but increases lead time and procurement overhead.
- Key audit asks: SOC 2 report (recent), BAA, data retention policy, network topology diagram, and optional on-prem checklist if customer leans that direction.

Proposed action items (who/when)
1) Redwood provides SOC 2 summary + latest report redacted for external review — owner: Marissa — requested by Tue 11/24 EOD. [attachment: redwood-soc2-summary-2026.pdf]
2) Draft BAA for Lifecore review — owner: Ben/Legal — I will circulate a BAA template and we can route to their legal/ procurement. [attachment: BAA-template-Redwood.docx]
3) Short runbook comparing tradeoffs (latency/unit cost/lead time) between Hosted, Dedicated, Private — owner: Karthik — deliverable: spreadsheet + recommended path for PHI use cases. [attachment: lifecore-map-draft.xlsx]
4) Procurement follow-up: request their standard timelines and any additional compliance checklist items — owner: Alex / Lifecore procurement — request: indicate whether Dedicated SLA and Typed PKI are required.

Questions I still have for you (so we scope evidence precisely)
- Will Lifecore require HSM-backed key management (KMS/HSM) for production keys, or is cloud KMS acceptable?
- Are there specific retention/PII deletion windows we must enforce by policy?
- Is there a requirement for on-prem deployment (air-gapped) for specific workflows or only regional VPC isolation?

Next practical step: I will send the SOC2 summary and BAA template by EOD Monday; Karthik will attach a short hosting-comparison sheet by Tuesday. If Lifecore prefers a canary on Dedicated for a 30-day window while we prepare a VPC deployment plan, we can scope that in the mutual action plan.

Thanks — I’ll follow up once the SOC2 summary is uploaded to the shared Drive link below.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0124
Redwood Inference — developer-first inference runtime

Attachments:
- redwood-soc2-summary-2026.pdf (summary, redacted sections)
- BAA-template-Redwood.docx

From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@lifecore.health>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@lifecore.health>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:17:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Lifecore: hosting eligibility & audit evidence — post-call workplan

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few points from Lifecore side: 

- Procurement timeline: we typically need vendor security evidence within 5 business days for initial review. If we can get the SOC2 summary + draft BAA by Tuesday that would keep us on schedule.
- KMS: cloud KMS (AWS KMS or GCP KMS) is acceptable for now, but for PHI-in-flight keys our security team may ask for HSM-backed keys during production sign-off — flagging this as a potential blocker.
- Retention: default retention is 30 days for logs and 90 days for derived PHI artifacts; deletion-by-request is required within 7 business days.
- On-prem: not required today; VPC with customer-controlled subnets is acceptable as an intermediate step.

Procurement is looped in here — procurement, please let us know if you need Redwood's vendor form or an MSSP reference.

— Alex
Alex Morgan
Head of Product Operations | Lifecore Health
alex.morgan@lifecore.health | +1 (212) 555-1010

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@lifecore.health>, Procurement <procurement@lifecore.health>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 08:07:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Lifecore: hosting eligibility & audit evidence — post-call workplan

Forwarding Alex's confirmation and procurement notes — key items to action for Redwood legal and solutions. See inline.

> Alex: cloud KMS acceptable; HSM likely requested at production sign-off. Retention windows: logs 30d, PHI artifacts 90d; deletion-by-request within 7 business days. VPC is acceptable short-term.

Marissa / Karthik — can you confirm:
1) If we provide the SOC2 report redacted + SOC2 summary, will that cover their 5-business-day initial vendor review?
2) Can the Dedicated offering be configured to use a customer-managed KMS at deploy time (we support BYOK flows)? If so, what ETA to include in the MAP?
3) If Lifecore asks for HSM, what is our recommended path (Dedicated with HSM, or Private)? Approx timeline and cost delta please.

I’ve attached the three files we discussed; cc'd procurement for any vendor-form asks.

Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@lifecore.health>, Procurement <procurement@lifecore.health>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Lifecore: hosting eligibility & audit evidence — post-call workplan

Thanks Ben — answered inline and added concrete next steps.

1) SOC2 evidence: yes — we will upload a redacted SOC 2 Type II report and a one-page summary to the shared Drive by EOD today (24 Nov). That should satisfy Lifecore's initial vendor review window. Action owner: Marissa. Link: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/lifecore-evidence

2) Dedicated + KMS/BYOK: we support BYOK for Dedicated (customer imports keys to cloud KMS or we configure a customer-managed key policy). ETA: we can have BYOK enabled for a Dedicated pilot within 10 business days after contract signature / key handoff. Action owner: Karthik (technical lead), timeframe to include in MAP.

3) HSM requirement: if Lifecore insists on FIPS 140-2 Level 3 HSM-backed keys for production, our recommended approach is Dedicated with HSM-integrated KMS or Private on-prem (longer runway). Rough estimates: Dedicated+HSM add ~3–4 weeks setup and a 12–18% cost uplift vs standard Dedicated; Private on-prem adds 8–12 weeks and >40% uplift depending on hardware procurement and install. These are preliminary — we will surface exact numbers in the MAP. Action owner: Karthik for detailed ETA/cost delta.

4) BAAs & procurement: Ben, please route the BAA-template to Alex's procurement contact; we'll accept counterchanges but ask for tracked redlines. If procurement needs references (MSSP or customer reference for similar PHI deployments), we can provide a short contact list.

5) Next meeting: propose a 30-minute technical sync (Redwood solutions + Lifecore security) to go over KMS options and deployment timelines. Suggested slots: Thu 11/26 10:00–10:30 PST or Fri 11/27 09:00–09:30 PST. Alex/procurement, please confirm availability.

I will start drafting the MAP spreadsheet (living doc) and populate the Dedicated vs Private line items this morning.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-2244
